Unlike [Pre-Classified Splatting](5410-pre-classified-splatting.md), which applies optical properties before projection and results in fuzzy edges due to kernel smoothing, this method preserves crisp object boundaries by deferring classification until after the density footprint is rasterized [S1, unofficial][S2, abstract only, unofficial][S3, unofficial].

The claim states that unlike Pre-Classified Splatting (which applies optical properties before projection, causing fuzzy edges), the described method preserves crisp boundaries by deferring classification until after the density footprint is rasterized. Source [S1] explicitly states that traditional splatting (pre-classified/pre-shaded) classifies and shades prior to projection, leading to blurry edges, and that the new method performs classification and shading after projection to render objects with crisp edges. Source [S2] confirms that post-shaded splatting (classification after projection) solves the blurry appearance inherent in traditional splatting. Source [S3] visually and textually contrasts 'Pre-Classified Rendering' (Classify -> Splat) with 'Post-Classified Rendering' (Splat -> Classify), noting that the latter yields a 'crisp edge image' while the former results in a 'blurred edge' due to the Gaussian kernel reconstruction. All facts in the claim are supported by the provided evidence.
supported
